whatItIs.text: Sweet corn is the sugar-rich fresh form of maize; the kernels are the grains of a tall grass, eaten on or off the cob.

historyNote.text: Maize was domesticated by indigenous peoples in southern Mexico about 9,000 years ago from wild teosinte, and traditionally planted with beans and squashes as the Three Sisters.

howToChoose.text: Choose cobs with bright green husks, moist pale silk, and tight rows of plump kernels that ooze milky juice when pressed.

storage.text: Refrigerate with husks on and eat as soon as you can.

useItUp.text: Stand cobs in the fridge; once kernels lose juice, cut them off for fritters, corn chowder, or a quick pan-charred side.

substitutions.note: convenient year-round; skip the cob but the sweetness holds
